newsitem.title: UK: UK private prisons should develop further -MPs.
newsitem.headline: UK private prisons should develop further -MPs.

text.p: The idea of privately-managed prisons is proving a success in Britain and should be developed further, an all-party committee of parliament said on Wednesday.
A report from the Home Affairs Committee said firms running four of Britain's low-security jails are saving the taxpayer money while performing at least as well as their state counterpart.
"The idea of privately managed prisons is undoubtedly now more generally accepted, and should be allowed to develop further," the report said.
The Wolds Prison in Humberside, northeast England, became the first to be privately run in Britain in 1992 when Group 4, part of private Dutch firm Group 4 Securitas, took charge.

Other companies currently involved in the field are UK Detention Services, whose main shareholder is Corrections Corp of America, and Premier Prisons, a joint venture between Wackenhut Corrections Corp and Serco Group Plc.
In addition, Securicor Group Plc leads a joint venture which will run one of the three private prisons currently under construction.

The report noted the government has a target for 10 percent of prisons to become privately run, but said if the 12 new prisons currently required were all put in the private sector, the figure would be 15 percent.
It said there had been early "teething troubles" in the first privately run prisons, notably a high level of assaults on staff.

But it added: "Privately managed prisons are now operating well in terms of the quality of performance and the regimes they run...Their performance overall has been at least as good as that of publicly run prisons and in some areas better."

Noting Home Office estimates that privately run prisons cost some 11 percent less per prisoner, the committee said although it was clear there were savings, it was premature to be specific about their extent. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
